title: Sulforaphane attenuates oxidative stress and vascular remodeling in indium lung disease rats via mediating the NF-kappaB and Nrf2 pathways.
authors: Wan, Peng; Cao, Fuyuan; Li, Gai; Hao, Xiaohui; Mu, Yu; Sun, Jian; Xue, Ling; Liu, Nan
one_liner_zh: 该文研究萝卜硫素经NF-kappaB/Nrf2通路缓解铟肺病大鼠氧化应激与血管重塑，虽含分子对接但核心为毒理与病理机制，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Indium lung disease is characterized by interstitial pneumonia, pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (PAP), pulmonary fibrosis, and lung cancer. However, this is insofar irreversible. The disease is believed to be caused by inhalation of indium and its compounds. We constructed a rat model of indium lung disease to explore the possible role of the NF-kappaB/Nrf2 pathway in indium‑tin oxide nanoparticle (Nano-ITO)-induced pulmonary injury and to reveal the regulatory mechanism. To integrate computational network toxicology and molecular docking with a rat model to identify core molecular targets and pathways underpinning ITO toxicity, and evaluate whether modulation of the NF-kappaB/Nrf2 axis by sulforaphane or all-trans retinoic acid mitigates Nano-ITO-induced lung injury. Toxicity prediction, target mining and integration with oxidative stress and vascular remodeling gene sets identified intersection targets that were analyzed by PPI, GO/KEGG/Reactome enrichment and topological analysis to select core nodes. Molecular docking probed interactions between ITO components and proteins in NF-kappaB/Nrf2 pathways. Next, we evaluated the NF-kappaB/Nrf2 signaling pathway to elucidate the molecular mechanism of sulforaphane in regulating inflammation, oxidative stress, vascular remodeling, vascular hyperplasia, PAP, cholesterol accumulation, and interstitial fibrosis in indium lung disease induced by Nano-ITO. Findings show that the NF-kappaB/Nrf2 signaling pathway is involved in Nano-ITO-induced vascular remodeling, cholesterol crystal formation, alveolar protein deposition, collagen hyperplasia, and interstitial fibrosis in rats. Sulforaphane can effectively attenuate Nano-ITO-induced inflammation, oxidative stress and vascular remodeling, as manifested by decreased expression of CD31, alpha-SMA, Collagen I, SP-A, SP-D, and inflammatory cytokine, via activating Nrf2 and inhibiting the NF-kappaB signaling pathway.
abstract_zh: 铟肺病以间质性肺炎、肺泡蛋白沉积症（PAP）、肺纤维化和肺癌为特征，但迄今为止该病不可逆。该病被认为由吸入铟及其化合物引起。我们构建了铟肺病大鼠模型，以探讨NF-kappaB/Nrf2通路在铟锡氧化物纳米颗粒（Nano-ITO）诱导的肺损伤中的可能作用，并揭示其调控机制。结合计算网络毒理学和分子对接与大鼠模型，以识别支撑ITO毒性的核心分子靶点和通路，并评估通过萝卜硫素或全反式维甲酸调节NF-kappaB/Nrf2轴是否能减轻Nano-ITO诱导的肺损伤。通过毒性预测、靶点挖掘以及与氧化应激和血管重塑基因集的整合，识别交集靶点，并采用PPI、GO/KEGG/Reactome富集和拓扑分析选择核心节点。分子对接探测了ITO组分与NF-kappaB/Nrf2通路中蛋白质之间的相互作用。接下来，我们评估了NF-kappaB/Nrf2信号通路，以阐明萝卜硫素在调节Nano-ITO诱导的铟肺病中炎症、氧化应激、血管重塑、血管增生、PAP、胆固醇积累和间质纤维化的分子机制。结果表明，NF-kappaB/Nrf2信号通路参与Nano-ITO诱导的大鼠血管重塑、胆固醇晶体形成、肺泡蛋白沉积、胶原增生和间质纤维化。萝卜硫素可通过激活Nrf2并抑制NF-kappaB信号通路，有效减轻Nano-ITO诱导的炎症、氧化应激和血管重塑，表现为CD31、α-SMA、Collagen I、SP-A、SP-D和炎症细胞因子表达降低。
